studies.label: Mathematical creativity tasks with ChatGPT, Google Search, or a human peer

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Sections 3.1 and 3.2; PDF p. 4, Table 1 arm headings
counts_source.quote: A total of 230 Chinese university students participated in this study. ... Human–ChatGPT (N = 60) Human–Google (N = 60) Human–Human (N = 110, 55 dyads) ... Each participant completed all the required tasks, and none were excluded.

arms.name: Human–ChatGPT
arms.description: Student completes the MCT with ChatGPT in one browser tab; instructed about prompting, adding context, refining responses, and uploading images or documents (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Human–Google
arms.description: Student completes the MCT with Google Search only; other AI tools and search engines are blocked (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Human–human
arms.description: Students work in randomly formed pairs; person A leads and person B supports without completing work independently. The arm contains 110 participants in 55 dyads, but the source does not identify whether analyzed creativity scores represent the joint dyad or person A alone (PDF p. 3, Sections 3.1 and 3.2; PDF p. 4, Table 1; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 6.1).

studies.task: After a solo number-pyramid baseline, students generate multiple solutions to four open-ended mathematical tasks involving grid figures, marble dispersion, water in a tilted prism, and shared geometric features, with their assigned partner (PDF pp. 3-5, Sections 3.1 and 4.1-4.2).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (model version not stated)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1 Procedure; neither a model version nor its release year is stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration or registry is mentioned in the saved paper.

studies.shared_sample: Possible overlap with c471, Liu et al. (2026), Exploring the impact of ChatGPT on college students' mathematical creativity: A quasi-experimental study, doi:10.14742/ajet.10564, as flagged in the reconciled screening form's sample_overlap. The form reports matching ChatGPT-arm demographics and tasks but different creativity summaries. The present paper does not confirm reuse or independence; no shared-participant count is established.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Hand-coded number of correct answer categories, summed across the four MCT tasks. Two scorers marked and categorized responses and resolved discrepancies. These are category counts, not subjective creativity ratings (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 5).

sources.quote: Human–ChatGPT (N = 60) Human–Google (N = 60) ... Each participant completed all the required tasks, and none were excluded.

estimates.notes: Table 3 column order is Human–ChatGPT, Human–Google, Human–human, with M and SD for each arm. The source quote retains the three arm pairs to preserve that ordering and printed precision; only the named treatment and control columns are transcribed into stats. No pairwise between-arm test is printed; the omnibus tests and within-arm changes are not this contrast. Both arms contribute participant-level summed scores. se_basis is participant because the available uncertainty inputs are participant-level arm SDs and participant counts; a direct pairwise SE or interval is not reported. n_total is null because the paper does not print a total specifically for this contrast.

The proportion of each category relative to all responses determines points: (0, 1%), (1%, 2%), or (2%, 3%) receives three, two, or one point, respectively; intervals are retained exactly as printed. Scores are summed across the four MCT tasks. Two scorers coded responses and resolved discrepancies (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 5).

not_extracted.what: Within-arm baseline-to-MCT changes in flexibility, fluency, and originality
not_extracted.reason: These paired tests compare a solo baseline with a later, different task under the same assigned partner condition. Condition order was not randomized and these are not randomized between-arm contrasts (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; PDF p. 4, Section 3.3; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 6.1).

not_extracted.what: Prior mathematical competence and its ANCOVA associations with the MCT outcomes
not_extracted.reason: Mathematical competence is a baseline characteristic, and the reported ANCOVA tests concern its association with creativity rather than a pairwise effect of assigned AI assistance (PDF p. 4, Table 1 and Section 3.3; PDF p. 8, Section 6.1).

not_extracted.what: Exploratory correlations among actual performance, self-evaluation, perceived usefulness, difficulty, effort, and self-efficacy
not_extracted.reason: Non-randomized within-condition associations involving self-reports, not full-sample randomized AI contrasts. The main text describes these on PDF pp. 11-12, Sections 7.3-7.5, citing an external appendix that was not available for inspection.
Elapsed study duration is not creativity or diversity scored on the produced solutions (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).

open_items: The human-peer arm's people-to-score mapping is not stated: joint-dyad scores versus person A's scores, the number of people represented in the creativity analysis, and the treatment of individual baselines remain unresolved. Its analyzed-person count, the overall analyzed-person count, and the peer contrasts' common unit and SD level are null (PDF pp. 3-4 and 7-8).

No pairwise between-arm SE, confidence interval, p-value, or standardized effect is printed for the eligible outcomes. Participant-level means, SDs, and arm counts are available for ChatGPT versus Google; peer contrasts additionally need a resolved analysis unit and valid uncertainty (PDF p. 7, Table 3; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 6.1).
The ChatGPT model version and release year are not reported; year is null (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).

The external Supporting Information appendix was not obtained. The main text identifies scoring reference tables and exploratory correlation Tables A1 and A3 (PDF pp. 6, 11-12 and 16), but its full contents cannot be confirmed. No matching supplement was found in the local literature search. urllib requests to the Wiley full article and Crossref DOI API, using User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, both failed with WinError 10013 (socket access blocked).

Possible sample overlap with c471 is unresolved. The reconciled form flags matching demographics and tasks, but the present paper does not establish whether the participants were reused. Sample deduplication requires confirmation.
The lottery slot configuration and allocation probabilities are not specified, despite an explicit description of individual random assignment (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).
notes: Extracted on 2026-10-10. The full markdown was read from start to end, including references and the Supporting Information notice. All cited PDF pages were extracted with pymupdf; the outcome rows were also checked with borderless table recovery. The quasi-experimental title does not override the explicit individual lottery assignment in Section 3.1. The reported lottery-group composition is used for randomized counts; no separate count at the draw is printed. The no-exclusion statement supports the analyzed counts in the two individual arms but does not resolve the peer arm's mapping from people to scores. The design is between participants; the common baseline-then-partner sequence was not randomized, so within_person is null. Table 3 reports raw outcome means and SDs; the mixed ANOVA uses z-standardized scores. Its omnibus F tests, partial eta-squared values and p-values cover all three conditions, and the reported t tests and Cohen's d values are within-arm changes. None is assigned to the pairwise estimates. Pairwise n_total values are null because no analyzed-person total for those two-arm contrasts is printed; no counts are calculated from arm sums or degrees of freedom. Descriptions of solution diversity refer to within-person flexibility, not a measured across-people diversity outcome. No effect, SE, interval, or missing count has been computed.
